\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آغاز} (âghâz)}{آغاز (âghâz)}]{\fa{آغاز} (âghâz) — a beginning, a start}

\label{lesson:FA-C302-aghaz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to take place, then the Persian for to last.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آغاز}}
\textbf{\fa{آغاز}} (\emph{âghâz}) — \textquotedblleft{}a beginning, a start\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آغاز} \fa{کلاس} \fa{ساعت} \fa{هشت} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Âghâz-e kelâs sâ'at-e hasht ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The start of the class is at eight o'clock.
\end{quote}

More formal than \emph{shoru'}. \emph{Dar âghâz} \textquotedblleft{}at the beginning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âghâz} is a native Persian word. EtymDB lists it without a parent, and its deeper origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âghâz}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âghâz}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{âghâz}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to take place, then the Persian for to last, then say \emph{âghâz} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{آغاز} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A beginning, a start\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آغاز} \fa{شدن} (âghâz shodan)}{آغاز شدن (âghâz shodan)}]{\fa{آغاز} \fa{شدن} (âghâz shodan) — to begin, to start (formal)}

\label{lesson:FA-C302-aghaz-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to last, then the Persian for a beginning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آغاز} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{آغاز} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{âghâz shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to begin, to start (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{جشن} \fa{ساعت} \fa{هفت} \fa{شب} \fa{آغاز} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Jashn sâ'at-e haft-e shab âghâz shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The celebration began at seven in the evening.
\end{quote}

The thing itself begins: \emph{âghâz mishavad}. With a doer the verb is \emph{âghâz kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to begin something\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âghâz shodan} joins \emph{âghâz} \textquotedblleft{}a beginning\textquotedblright{}, a native word whose deeper origin is not settled, with \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}, inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âghâz shodan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âghâz shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{âghâz shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to last, then the Persian for a beginning, then say \emph{âghâz shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{آغاز} \fa{شدن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To begin, to start (formal)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پایان} (pâyân)}{پایان (pâyân)}]{\fa{پایان} (pâyân) — an end, an ending}

\label{lesson:FA-C302-payan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a beginning, then the Persian for to begin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پایان}}
\textbf{\fa{پایان}} (\emph{pâyân}) — \textquotedblleft{}an end, an ending\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پایان} \fa{فیلم} \fa{را} \fa{دوست} \fa{نداشتم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pâyân-e film râ dust nadâshtam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I did not like the end of the film.
\end{quote}

\emph{Dar pâyân} \textquotedblleft{}in the end\textquotedblright{}; \emph{be pâyân residan} \textquotedblleft{}to come to an end\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pâyân} is a native Persian word, usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{pāyān}, \textquotedblleft{}end\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pâyân}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pâyân}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{pâyân}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a beginning, then the Persian for to begin, then say \emph{pâyân} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{پایان} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An end, an ending\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پایان} \fa{یافتن} (pâyân yâftan)}{پایان یافتن (pâyân yâftan)}]{\fa{پایان} \fa{یافتن} (pâyân yâftan) — to come to an end}

\label{lesson:FA-C302-payan-yaftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to begin, then the Persian for an end.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پایان} \fa{یافتن}}
\textbf{\fa{پایان} \fa{یافتن}} (\emph{pâyân yâftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to come to an end\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{جنگ} \fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{هشت} \fa{سال} \fa{پایان} \fa{یافت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Jang ba'd az hasht sâl pâyân yâft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The war came to an end after eight years.
\end{quote}

Formal; in speech \emph{tamâm shod}. Present stem \emph{yâb-}: \emph{pâyân miyâbad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pâyân yâftan} joins \emph{pâyân} \textquotedblleft{}end\textquotedblright{} and \emph{yâftan} \textquotedblleft{}to find, to attain\textquotedblright{}, both native Persian words: literally \textquotedblleft{}to find an end\textquotedblright{}. EtymDB lists neither.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سرانجام} (saranjâm)}{سرانجام (saranjâm)}]{\fa{سرانجام} (saranjâm) — finally, at last}

\label{lesson:FA-C302-saranjam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an end, then the Persian for to come to an end.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سرانجام}}
\textbf{\fa{سرانجام}} (\emph{saranjâm}) — \textquotedblleft{}finally, at last\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سرانجام} \fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{سه} \fa{ساعت} \fa{به} \fa{خانه} \fa{رسیدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Saranjâm ba'd az se sâ'at be khâne residim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Finally, after three hours, we reached home.
\end{quote}

Written and storytelling Persian; in speech \emph{bel-akhare}. Also a noun, \textquotedblleft{}outcome\textquotedblright{}: \emph{saranjâm-e kâr} \textquotedblleft{}the outcome of the affair\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{saranjâm} joins \emph{sar} \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{} and \emph{anjâm} \textquotedblleft{}end, completion\textquotedblright{}, both native Persian words. EtymDB lists the compound with no parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an end, then the Persian for to come to an end, then say \emph{saranjâm} again
\end{itemize}
